briefs.headline: Herfurth's nine saves carry No. 16 WVU past No. 20 BYU
briefs.summary: Sophia Nickel scored twice after halftime and Bailey Herfurth made nine saves as WVU women's soccer beat BYU 2-0 Thursday in Morgantown, three points behind Big 12 leader Texas Tech.

briefs.headline: Ravenswood beats Hannan 5-1 in non-league match at Ashton
briefs.summary: Ravenswood scored five on the Golden Wave Thursday at Hannan High School in a non-league match not on the coach's schedule; MaxPreps posted the 5-1 final with no scorer. Hannan is at Point Pleasant JV Friday, 6 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Tottenham's Simons enrolls at Harvard during ACL rehab
briefs.summary: Xavi Simons, 23, said on LinkedIn he was accepted onto Harvard Business School's online Crossover Into Business program while rehabbing an ACL tear; ESPN said he is not expected back before 2027.

briefs.headline: Chase returns to Bengals practice; Higgins misses second day
briefs.summary: Cincinnati's Thursday report lists Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) as limited after missing Wednesday, while Tee Higgins (groin, neck), Kyle Dugger and Jonathan Allen did not practice; B.J. Hill was limited (Achilles).

briefs.headline: Browns' Graham and Hall miss a second straight practice
briefs.summary: Cleveland's Thursday report lists DT Mason Graham (knee, ankle), DT Mike Hall Jr., G Teven Jenkins and WR Tylan Wallace as did-not-participate before Sunday at the Jets; DE Derek Barnett was limited.

briefs.headline: Marshall's Clark out for Coastal after JMU hospital trip
briefs.summary: Wednesday's Sun Belt availability report lists linebacker Chason Clark out for Saturday's 7 p.m. ET game against Coastal Carolina; Clark left the James Madison game by ambulance and was released from the hospital Sunday.

briefs.headline: Hawks beat Spurs 123-116 in San Antonio's preseason opener
briefs.summary: Atlanta scored 42 second-quarter points to erase a 19-point deficit Thursday at Frost Bank Center; Dylan Harper led the Spurs with 16 points, Victor Wembanyama had 9 points and 6 rebounds in 17 minutes and De'Aaron Fox did not play.

briefs.headline: Guardians beat White Sox 9-5 to force ALDS Game 5
briefs.summary: Jose Ramirez homered and drove in three and Cleveland scored six in the sixth Thursday to square the series at two games each. Game 5 is Saturday at 8 p.m. ET in Cleveland; the winner meets Tampa Bay Monday.

briefs.headline: Irving runs for 165 as Buccaneers beat Cowboys 24-16
briefs.summary: Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels went 19 of 25 for 189 yards for Baker Mayfield and Tampa Bay rushed for 241 Thursday for its first win in five games. Dak Prescott threw two interceptions.

briefs.headline: Payton and Ryans take over play-calling for slumping units
briefs.summary: Denver's Sean Payton said Thursday he will call offensive plays from Sunday's game against the Chargers. Houston's DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday he is taking defensive calls from Matt Burke with the Texans winless in four.

briefs.headline: Stankoven hat trick carries Hurricanes past Canucks 7-2
briefs.summary: Logan Stankoven's first career hat trick came short-handed, on the power play and at even strength Thursday; Andrei Svechnikov added two goals as Carolina won its third straight.

briefs.headline: Vegas rallies from three down to beat Leafs 4-3 in shootout
briefs.summary: Toronto led by three Thursday before Jack Eichel scored on a penalty shot and Vegas tied it; Trevor Connelly won it in the fifth round. Sergei Bobrovsky made 40 saves for the Leafs.

briefs.headline: Man City appeal guilty verdict on 100-plus charges before Anfield trip
briefs.summary: Manchester City have appealed an independent commission's guilty verdict on more than 100 Premier League financial charges covering 2009 to 2018, Al Jazeera reported Thursday; sanctions could run from a points deduction to expulsion. Sunday at Liverpool is City's first match since.

briefs.headline: UEFA sets criteria for a challenger to Infantino
briefs.summary: After its 55 federations met Thursday, UEFA said it wants "a respected and unifying figure, deeply rooted in football" to run for FIFA president in March; Aleksander Ceferin will not stand, AP reported.

briefs.headline: Bordeaux relegated to France's sixth tier over its finances
briefs.summary: The six-time French champions, sold last month for one euro to U.S. group Park Bench, will play in the sixth division this season, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league confirmed Thursday, AFP reported.

briefs.headline: Rahm quits LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms
briefs.summary: Lawyer John Beck told a bankruptcy hearing Wednesday that the two-time major champion reviewed the proposed "LIV 2.0" terms and will not take part, Reuters reported.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu joins autumn tour Saturday after knee surgery
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, 27, who had right-knee surgery in late July and sat out September's basho (tournament), rejoins the jungyo (regional tour) at Matsumoto on Saturday, tour chief Takadagawa said Friday, Nikkan Sports reported.

briefs.headline: Yoshinofuji resumes bouts with a Kyushu homecoming in mind
briefs.summary: Maegashira (rank-and-file) Yoshinofuji, 25, from Uto in Kumamoto, whose family home was ruled destroyed by July's earthquake, won four of seven practice bouts Friday at Chichibu and said he wants to win for home fans at the Kyushu basho (tournament) in November.

sections.label: On the Water
sections.note: All four waters reported from the locked fishing.json, generated_at 2026-10-09T05:44:02-04:00, errors list empty; the file was not re-run by this desk and every figure is printed as it stands there. The fetcher's '24h ago' comparison points on all three USGS gauges are again the first point of its two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Wednesday reading, not the true 24-hour mark: a direct pull of the 4:30-7 a.m. Wednesday points at 5:51 a.m. shows Williams 71.4 cfs and 1.46 feet, Point Pleasant 24.35 and Huntington 26.17 all sitting at exactly 5:45 a.m. Wednesday, while the true marks are Williams 62.8 cfs and 1.40 feet at 5:15 a.m. Thursday, Point Pleasant 24.80 at 5 a.m. Thursday and Huntington 25.85 at 5 a.m. Thursday (each is Thursday's edition reading). Williams: falling flag right on the day, down 7.9 cfs and 0.06 feet in an unbroken recession, and right at the hour by one gauge step (56.2 at 1 a.m. to 54.9 at 3:15, flat since), though the fetcher's 16.5-cfs drop is about twice the true one; 54.9 cfs is the low of the two-day window, the lowest reading of the recession from the Sept. 23 crest of 1,450 cfs, and the lowest since the 56.2 of Sept. 18, three weeks ago, which makes this the 11th morning of prime wading water. Point Pleasant: rising flag right on the day by nine hundredths, up from 24.80, and right at the hour, the pool having climbed from a window low of 24.11 at 3 p.m. Thursday through 24.61 at 11 p.m. to 24.89 at 4:45 and 5 a.m., with a 24.92 spike at 3:15; the fetcher's comparison makes the rise look like 0.54 against a true 0.09. Huntington: steady flag wrong on the day, up 0.25 from Thursday's 25.85, and right at the hour, the gauge chopping between 26.03 and 26.21 since 2 a.m. and down five hundredths in the last quarter hour inside the usual lockage chop. The Summersville release stepped UP on the USGS trace Thursday evening: 03189600 below the dam, stage only (its discharge series carried no values), held 7.73-7.74 feet from 5 a.m. Thursday through 7:15 p.m., then 7.79 at 8 p.m., 8.40 at 8:15, 8.47 at 8:45, 9.28 at 9:15, 9.47 at 9:45, 10.06 at 10, 10.50 at 10:15, 10.79 at 11 and 11.02 at 11:15 p.m., and has held 11.01-11.04 since, 11.04 at 4:45 a.m., a 3.3-foot rise in three stages; the Gauley above Belva (03192000) had not yet seen it at 5 a.m., 479 cfs at 5 a.m. Thursday easing to 461 cfs and 1.83 feet from 9:30 p.m. through 5 a.m., the window's low and flat; 03189100, the Gauley near Craigsville above the lake, read 219 cfs and 10.53 feet from 2:15 through 4:30 a.m. against 254 Thursday. Those are readings of the USGS traces pulled at 5:49 a.m., not Corps statements; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened, so no lake level and no release figure is printed. NWS at 5:50 a.m.: no product active anywhere in West Virginia; nothing for Coastal Pender (NCZ106) or Coastal New Hanover (NCZ108). NWS Wilmington's only product is a Coastal Flood Advisory for Inland New Hanover, the lower Cape Fear including downtown Wilmington, 8 to 11 a.m., up to a half foot of inundation on the morning high, which is not Topsail water, so the Topsail block carries no beach-weather line; the Gulf storm Isaias has no NWS product on this coast. USNO phases API answered this morning: new moon Saturday, Oct. 10, 15:50 UT, re-verified; first quarter Oct. 18, full Oct. 26.

waters.reading: 54.9 cfs, 1.34 feet at 5:15 a.m., flagged falling against 71.4 cfs and 1.46 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Eleven mornings of prime wading water, and the thinnest the river has been since Sept. 18. The USGS two-day trace, pulled at 5:49 a.m., runs the river down a step every few hours with no rise in it: 62.8 cfs and 1.40 feet at 5:15 a.m. Thursday, the true 24-hour mark and Thursday's edition reading, 62.8 through 8:45 a.m., 61.5 from 9 a.m. through 12:30 p.m., 60.1 from 12:45 through 4 p.m., 58.8 at 4:15 with a 60.1 flicker at 4:30, 58.8 from 4:45 through 8:30 p.m., 57.5 from 8:45 p.m. to midnight, 56.2 at 12:15 a.m. with a 57.5 flicker at 12:30, 56.2 from 1 through 3 a.m., then 54.9 cfs and 1.34 feet from 3:15 through 5:15 a.m., the window's low. Against the true 24-hour mark that is down 7.9 cfs and 0.06 feet on the day, so the fetcher's falling flag is right on the day and right at the hour by a single gauge step, the river now sitting two hours on one reading. Its 71.4 cfs and 1.46 feet comparison point is the first point of its own two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Wednesday reading (a direct pull of the Wednesday dawn points puts 71.4 and 1.46 at 5:15 through 7 a.m. Wednesday, and Wednesday's edition recorded the same pair at 5:15), not 24 hours ago; it makes the drop look like 16.5 cfs, about twice the true 7.9. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, prime wading water. What 55 cfs means: it is the lowest number of the whole run down from the Sept. 23 crest of 1,450 cfs, 16 days of recession, the lowest since the 56.2 of Sept. 18, and within a few cfs of the 47.6 and 44.2 the river touched Sept. 10-11 before the September rains, so this is late-summer base flow in the second week of October, the pocket water reduced to the plunge-pool heads and the undercuts, and the fish concentrated and spooky. The Weather Service's active list for West Virginia carried no product at 5:50 a.m., no frost advisory for Pocahontas, where the river rises, and no fog statement. At 55 cfs and clear, the river is a long-leader, small-fly problem and nothing else: a 12-foot leader to 6X or 7X, a size 18 or 20 Blue-Winged Olive or Parachute Adams over the tailouts once the sun is on the water and the olives start, a size 18 Pheasant Tail or Zebra Midge on a short dropper under the dry through the plunge-pool heads, where the fish hold in the only depth left, a size 16 soft hackle swung through the tailouts midday, and a size 12 or 14 October Caddis dry alone over the undercut banks in the last hour of light, the one big bite on the river; with the stonefly nymphs under the rocks rather than on the water in October, a small black stonefly nymph on the dropper is the other choice through the plunge pools. Approach from downstream, stay on the gravel, and make the first cast count, because at this flow every fish in a pool sees the wade; a small olive sculpin stripped tight to the undercuts is a last-light bet only on water this thin. WVDNR's fall trout guide page, opened again this morning and still last modified Sept. 15, says select streams and lakes will be stocked with large catchable-size trout during the weeks of Oct. 19 and Oct. 26, more than 40,000 pounds in about 40 lakes and streams, most of them one to two pounds, and names the Cranberry and the Elk among its picks, with 1,500 trout for the Elk and the Back Fork in November and December; the Williams is not named on that page.

The falling flag is right on the day and right at the hour. 54.9 cfs is the window's low and the lowest reading since Sept. 18. waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.89 feet at 5 a.m., flagged rising against 24.35 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.9 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up nine hundredths on the day and climbing since mid-afternoon Thursday, the pool back at the top of its band. The trace, pulled at 5:49 a.m., runs 24.80 at 5 a.m. Thursday, the true 24-hour mark and Thursday's edition reading, 24.74 at 5:45, 24.59 at 7, 24.36 at 8:30, 24.43 at 10, 24.31 at noon, 24.24 at 1:30 p.m., 24.40 at 2:45, the window's low of 24.11 at 3 p.m., 24.31 at 3:45, 24.37 at 4:45, 24.47 at 7, 24.52 at 10:30, 24.61 at 11 p.m. and midnight, 24.67 at 12:15 a.m., 24.69 at 1:30, 24.73 at 2, 24.77 at 3, a 24.92 spike at 3:15, 24.81 at 3:30, 24.83 and 24.84 from 3:45 through 4:30, and 24.89 at 4:45 and 5 a.m. That is up 0.09 on the day and up 0.28 since midnight, 0.06 in the last hour, so the fetcher's rising flag is right on the day and right at the hour. Its 24.35 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Wednesday reading (a direct pull of the Wednesday dawn points puts 24.35 at exactly 5:45 a.m. Wednesday), not 24 hours ago, and it makes the rise look like 0.54 against the true 0.09. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Upstream the Summersville release stepped up on the USGS trace Thursday evening: 03189600 below the dam, stage only, held 7.73 to 7.74 feet from 5 a.m. Thursday through 7:15 p.m., then climbed in three stages, 7.79 at 8 p.m., 8.40 at 8:15, 8.47 at 8:45, 9.28 at 9:15, 9.47 at 9:45, 10.06 at 10, 10.50 at 10:15, 10.79 at 11 and 11.02 at 11:15 p.m., and has held 11.01 to 11.04 since, 11.04 at 4:45 a.m., 3.3 feet above where it sat for the previous 36 hours and above the 9.44 it read Wednesday morning before the last cut; the Gauley above Belva, USGS 03192000, had not seen that water by 5 a.m., 479 cfs and 1.86 feet at 5 a.m. Thursday, 473 at 5:30, 467 from 10:30 a.m., and 461 cfs and 1.83 feet from 9:30 p.m. through 5 a.m., the window's low and flat for seven and a half hours. The Gauley near Craigsville, above the lake, read 219 cfs and 10.53 feet from 2:15 through 4:30 a.m. against 254 a day earlier, the inflow still easing. The Corps' Huntington District site was not opened, so no lake elevation and no Corps release figure is printed; the step-up is a reading of the USGS stage trace, not a Corps statement, and whatever it carries reaches Belva, the Kanawha and this pool over the day. At 24.9 with the pool flat-to-rising and the Gauley water behind it still a day off, the river fishes structure: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked across the wing dams, the fish on the downstream face and in the slack behind them, a half-ounce blade bait or a three-inch paddletail on a half-ounce head along the riprap at first light, a crawfish-pattern jig crawled down the riprap where it meets the mud for the smallmouth and the drum once the sun is up, and the lock wall at Byrd as the deep edge for the sauger and the hybrids on a jigging spoon or a live skipjack; cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark, with the new moon tomorrow making the nights the darkest of the month.
waters.note: This is the gauge above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, the pool side; the Byrd tailwater is not gauged by USGS and is not printed. The fetcher's 24.35 comparison point is the first point of its two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Wednesday reading, not 24 hours ago; the trace's true 24-hour mark is 24.80 at 5 a.m. Thursday, Thursday's edition reading. The rising flag is right on the day (by 0.09) and right at the hour. The Summersville step-up is read off USGS 03189600's stage trace, not from the Corps.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.1 feet at 5 a.m., flagged steady against 26.17 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.1 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up a quarter foot on the day inside the usual quarter-hour chop, and the steady flag is wrong on the day and right at the hour. The trace, pulled at 5:49 a.m., runs 25.85 at 5 a.m. Thursday, the true 24-hour mark and Thursday's edition reading, 25.94 at 6:30, 26.01 at 8:15, 26.12 at 9:15, 25.96 at noon, 25.85 at 12:15 p.m., 25.90 at 2, 26.00 at 3:15, 25.84 at 4, 26.02 at 4:30, 25.78 at 5:15 p.m., the window's low, 25.94 at 7, 25.99 at 9, 26.09 at 10:15, 26.12 at 11:15 p.m. and midnight, 26.14 at 1 a.m., 26.19 at 2, 26.21 at 2:15, the window's high, 26.08 at 3, 26.15 at 3:30, 26.03 at 3:45, 26.06 at 4, 26.16 at 4:15, 26.14 at 4:30, 26.15 at 4:45 and 26.10 at 5 a.m. That is up 0.25 on the day, so the fetcher's steady flag is wrong there, and flat to the chop at the hour, down five hundredths in the last quarter hour inside a band of two tenths it has held since 2 a.m., so the flag is right at the hour. Its 26.17 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 5:45 a.m. Wednesday reading (a direct pull of the Wednesday dawn points puts 26.17 at exactly 5:45 a.m. Wednesday), not 24 hours ago; it sits seven hundredths over today's number only because Wednesday dawn was near the top of the window. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. The Point Pleasant pool above drained to 24.11 at 3 p.m. Thursday and has climbed 0.78 since, to 24.89 at 5 a.m., and this gauge's overnight rise from 25.78 at 5:15 p.m. to 26.21 at 2:15 a.m. reads like the front of that water passing the dam; the Summersville release stepped up 3.3 feet on the USGS stage trace Thursday evening and had not reached Belva by 5 a.m. (see Point Pleasant), a reading of the USGS traces, not a Corps statement, and the quarter-hour chop reads like lockages. At 26.1 with more water coming through the dam than Thursday, the current below it is pulse current, and the fish will be on the eddy seams while a pulse runs and tucked into the rock when it slacks: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon swum along the downstream face of the wing dams and through the eddy seam below each one when water comes through, a half-ounce blade bait along the riprap for the sauger and the smallmouth in the low light, a crawfish-colored tube or jig on the riprap toe as the sun gets up, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark; the lock wall fishes from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when the gates open, and with the pool above rising and the Gauley step-up still upstream, the weekend should carry more current here than the week did.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 1:47 AM at 0.4 ft, high 7:41 AM at 4.3 ft, low 2:12 PM at 0.5 ft, high 8:02 PM at 4.1 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 12:40 AM at 0.2 ft, high 6:58 AM at 5.3 ft, low 1:09 PM at 0.1 ft, high 7:19 PM at 5.0 ft. Water 74.1F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon waning crescent, 4% lit, 27.6 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 7:41 AM and 8:02 PM in the sound.
waters.working: One day short of the new moon, 27.6 days old and 4 percent lit, the moon is gone from the sky and the spring tides are here: the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered again this morning, puts the new moon Saturday, Oct. 10, at 15:50 UT, 11:50 a.m. ET, with the first quarter Oct. 18 and the full moon Oct. 26, so today and tomorrow carry the biggest swings and the hardest inlet current of the month, and the most bait moving through it. The sound at Hampstead came off a 0.4-foot low at 1:47 a.m. and fills 3.9 feet to a 4.3-foot high at 7:41 a.m., slack high about an hour after first light; it then drains 3.8 feet to a 0.5-foot low at 2:12 p.m., so the last two hours of the morning ebb, about 12:15 to 2:12 p.m., land in full daylight, and fills 3.6 feet in just under six hours to a 4.1-foot high at 8:02 p.m., after dark, with the evening ebb running on through the night; all four sound events fall inside Friday. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water today: low 12:40 a.m. at 0.2, high 6:58 a.m. at 5.3, low 1:09 p.m. at 0.1, high 7:19 p.m. at 5.0, a 5.1- and 5.2-foot swing against Thursday's 4.7 and 4.8, the springs showing; today's lags from the two tables are 43 and 43 minutes on the highs and 67 and 63 minutes on the lows, the lows again lagging longer, the long-ebb pattern that stretches the drum window at the crew's spot. For their water two miles north of the inlet, tide stage first: the red drum window is the bottom of the morning ebb, roughly 12:15 to 2:12 p.m., in daylight and with more water leaving the marsh than on any ebb since the September full moon, and again on the evening ebb after 8:02 p.m. in the dark; the flood from 2:12 to 8:02 covers the oyster bars and grass edges and puts the drum in the flooded grass and under the docks around the 8:02 p.m. high; slack at 7:41 a.m., 2:12 p.m. and 8:02 p.m. is dead water. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 74.1 degrees at 5:36 a.m., up 0.7 from Thursday's 73.4 after the slide from Sunday's 79.5. What is running is eight days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:50 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings starting to show at the piers, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered through the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no real word on trout; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, a few trout on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jrs. and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds on shrimp at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp under popping corks, flounder as bycatch; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs. The piers: Jolly Roger reports tons of bait, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water: finger mullet and shrimp are the forage and the report says the mullet are in, so for the ebb window a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, and a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low; on the afternoon flood, a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they cover, then a topwater walked over the flooded grass and down the dock lines around the 8:02 p.m. high, with the dock lights the trout spot once the moonless dark sets in; a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead on either moving tide. Flounder are release only. On the beach side, Gotcha plugs and metal jigs under the birds on the morning high for the Spanish and the bluefish, and a 5.3-foot surf high at 6:58 a.m. with a stiff spring ebb behind it says the inlet mouth will run hard through mid-morning. Beach conditions: no product for Coastal Pender at 5:50 a.m.; NWS Wilmington's coastal flood advisory this morning is for the lower Cape Fear at Wilmington, not Topsail.
